title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page opens a 'programme' for crystalline Dieudonné theory of Barsotti–Tate (p-divisible) groups over a base S on which p is locally nilpotent.

(a) The Dieudonné functor. One wants a contravariant functor D*: BT(S)^op → Crisloclib(S), from BT groups over S to locally free crystals on the crystalline site of S relative to Z_p. It should commute with base change, i.e. be a cartesian functor on the fibred category of BT groups over bases where p is locally nilpotent.

Let S_0 = V(p) be the closed subscheme defined by p. Then S_0 → S is a nilpotent thickening and the ideal (p) carries its canonical divided powers. By topological invariance of the crystalline site, Crisloclib(S) ≃ Crisloclib(S_0). Hence D* is determined by its restriction BT(S_0)^op → Crisloclib(S_0), and D*(G) depends only on G_0 = G ×_S S_0. This reduces everything to characteristic p.

Over S_0 of characteristic p, use:
- the relative Frobenius f_G: G → G^(p) and the Verschiebung v_G: G^(p) → G;
- the compatibility of D* with the base change by absolute Frobenius f_S, which gives D*(G^(p)) = f_S^*(M) = M^(p).
Then M = D*(G_0) acquires F_M: M^(p) → M and V_M: M → M^(p), whose composites are multiplication by p.

Such a triple (M, F_M, V_M) is called an F-V-crystal, or Dieudonné crystal (marginal addition). The resulting D*: BT(S_0) → F-V-Cris(S_0) is 'the' Dieudonné functor. Its formation commutes with arbitrary base change. Over the spectrum of a perfect field it agrees, up to canonical isomorphism, with the classical Dieudonné functor, which is then an equivalence.

The next page draws the consequence: D*(G_0) recovers all fibres of G_0 at perfect points. It then poses Problem 1: is D* fully faithful over a characteristic-p base S_0, and is its essential image the 'admissible' F-V-crystals? Grothendieck suggests that settling this requires a Dieudonné theory of finite locally free p-group schemes. That theory would involve F-V-crystals with extra structure, probably a filtration on an object of a derived category.

This is the programme Grothendieck announced at ICM Nice 1970 and in the Montréal lectures (1970, published 1974). Messing (LNM 264), Mazur–Messing (LNM 370) and Berthelot–Breen–Messing (LNM 930) carried it out.
errors: With F_M: M^(p) → M and V_M: M → M^(p), and composition read right-to-left, V_M∘F_M is an endomorphism of M^(p) and F_M∘V_M is an endomorphism of M. The page writes V_M F_M = p·id_M and F_M V_M = p·id_{M^(p)}, so the subscripts are swapped. This is a harmless slip of convention.
The first display gives D*: BT(S)^o (contravariant), but the last display omits the ^o: D*: BT(S_0) → F-V-Cris(S_0). The variance notation is inconsistent; the functor is still contravariant.
'cf. plus haut' leaves a blank where a cross-reference was meant to go (the equivalence Crisloclib(S) ≃ Crisloclib(S_0) via topological invariance of the crystalline site).

deep.surprise_reason: This is a typescript draft of Grothendieck's well-known Barsotti–Tate/crystal programme, which he published at ICM 1970 and in the Montréal 1974 lectures, and which later work took up extensively (Messing, BBM, de Jong, Zink, Lau, prismatic theory). It is new only as a draft variant, e.g. the marginal naming 'cristal de Dieudonné'.
